facts.text: Nebius shares fell 16% on Thursday after the Amsterdam-based AI cloud company cut its outlook for this year.
Third-quarter revenue rose 571% from a year earlier, to $980.8m. Analysts surveyed by LSEG had expected $907.5m.
Nebius now expects 2026 revenue at the low end of its $3bn to $3.4bn range. For 2027, Nebius expects revenue of $12bn to $13bn.
The cut comes from delays at data centre sites that Nebius rents from other companies. Some capacity due this year has moved to the first half of 2027.
One of them is a 300MW site in Vineland, New Jersey, held up by delays in power.
Founder and chief executive Arkady Volozh: "Building at this scale is hard, and delays are part of our industry right now. We are not immune."
For 2027, Nebius plans to spend $40bn to $45bn, well above the $28.77bn analysts expected.

caption:
Nebius grew revenue 571% in a year, but data-centre delays cut its 2026 outlook and its shares fell 16%.

Nebius is an Amsterdam-based AI cloud company. Its results show AI demand and real-world building limits side by side.
